symptom: Inside a custom error handler, `describe microflow` printed nothing after an `if … end if;` ("The description goes from `end if;` straight to `end error;`") and printed a loop as its bare header (`loop $Order in $Orders`, no begin/body/end loop). No warning; `create or modify` said Unchanged; drop + create rerouted the handler's tail into the main flow (a failed call logged `done` and returned 1), `mx check` clean. The loop shape did not parse
cause: Two gaps in the handler walk (`collectErrorHandlerStatementSpans`), a second, smaller describer. (1) Its stop, `firstReachableErrorHandlerMerge`, was "the first merge with more than one way in" — and the merge closing an `if` in the handler body is exactly that, so it became the boundary and the split's continue-after-merge step was skipped (`nestedMergeID == boundary`). (2) It formatted a LoopedActivity with `formatActivity`, i.e. the header only, never calling `emitLoopBody`
insight: The handler's exit is the first merge with a way in from OUTSIDE the handler (any origin not reachable from the handler start over normal flows), not the first multi-entry merge; the old no-op-merge rule (#1078 follow-up) is the one-way-in special case of this. Ask which walk disagrees: the main describer and the handler walk each re-implement compound statements, and every shape the handler walk lacks (loop body here, nested custom handlers still) is a silent drop there. `assertDescriptionRebuildsGraph` caught the reroute as `invented flow … -> LogMessageAction(main)` — use it for every handler shape. Controls: dropping the `joinsOutside` check fails both if-tests, disabling the loop branch fails the loop test. E2E on 11.12.4: reporter's script, describe → drop+create → describe is byte-identical, `mxcli docker check` passes. Not fixed here: an `if` without `else` in a handler still prints an empty `else` (parses, rebuilds the same graph)
